title: OpenAI autolog tests use mock scenarios selected by the first message content
answers: how to add a mock OpenAI streaming error case for tests
where to add a fake OpenAI server response scenario
test OpenAI autolog stream error without calling the real API
body:
Convention: tests/openai/mock_openai.py serves fake OpenAI responses. A scenario is a module-level constant (e.g. EMPTY_STREAM, ERROR_MID_STREAM) and a matching elif branch in the chat() endpoint that keys on payload.messages[0].content.
Add new scenarios as a constant plus a branch there, then import the constant in tests/openai/test_openai_autolog.py.
Streaming tests in test_openai_autolog.py run against both sync and async clients; use client._is_async to choose between list(stream) and async iteration, and wrap the consume step in pytest.raises for error cases.
applies: Tests for the OpenAI autolog integration under tests/openai/.
says: Add automated tests for streaming chat errors without calling the real model service.
Verify that empty chat streams are tested using simulated server responses.
Test streaming autologging failure scenarios without making live external calls.
Ensure test coverage for interrupted chat completions using mock response scenarios.
search: OpenAI autolog test conventions use mock scenarios in tests/openai/mock_openai.py dispatched by the content of the first message in the chat endpoint. New fake server scenarios are added as module-level constants and elif branches matching payload.messages[0].content, then imported into tests/openai/test_openai_autolog.py. Streaming tests exercise both sync and async clients using client._is_async to toggle between list(stream) and async iteration, wrapping consumption in pytest.raises for error cases.
